limits: Static trace only: no captured instruction was executed and no concrete input values were observed.  The direct-access census covers the record register and the pinned alias registers of the twelve pinned bodies, at the embeddings the traced call sites establish; whole-record copies move bytes without naming fields -- copy destinations were reviewed in the level-0 and level-1 bodies and are stack buffers, register-held pointers, or record ranges outside the target offsets, apart from the two shaping copies recorded in the findings -- so for copied fields the census is a statement about direct accesses and the copies actually observed.  The caller bulk a 1 shaping arm is a jump-table arm: its relation to the twin call arm is not decidable from direct edges, and the packet records the writes and the arm structure without claiming which arm runs for a given record.  The b-side caller is reached only through its data slot; per-instruction provenance of the arena above that boundary is out of static reach for this packet.  The level-3 functions that call the level-2 bodies are censused for the caller sets but their bodies are not pinned.  The copy target at slot 0x64df508 is identified by argument shape only.  The decoder helper 0x2cd7ac0 is treated as the u64 reader established by the chain; the provenance of the bytes it decodes belongs to the payload producers.  Raw values are recorded mechanically; no field types are guessed.
